pr_title: Don't crash when the user tries to duplicate a tab with a profile that no longer exists
pr_body:
## Summary of the Pull Request

When the user tries to `duplicateTab` with a profile that doesn't exist anymore (like might happen after a settings reload), don't crash.

## PR Checklist
* [x] Closes #2455
* [x] I work here
* [x] Tests added/passed
* [n/a] Requires documentation to be updated
* [ ] Should we display an error dialog when this situation happens? 
  - Should this be a follow-up task?

## Detailed Description of the Pull Request / Additional comments

`CascadiaSettings::BuildSettings` can throw if the GUID doesn't exist. This wraps those calls up with a try/catch.

It also adds a couple tests - a few `SettingsTests` for try/catching this state. It also adds a XAML-y test in `TabTests` that creates a `TerminalPage` and then performs som UI-like actions on it. This test required a minor change to how we generate the new tab dropdown - in the tests, `Application::Current()` is _not_ a `TerminalApp::App`, so it doesn't have a `Logic()` to query. So wrap that in a try/catch as well.


## Validation Steps Performed
* Ran tests - new tests pass!
* Validated scenario manually

issue_context.title: Bug Report: Cannot find profile --> Crash
issue_context.body:
# Environment

Introduced by #2422 

Since we'll be defaulting to the Windows Terminal default settings, this means that the user may be working with profiles that don't exist AFTER the proper settings are imported. Below is an example of such a case, but several other places may cause the same issue to arise.

I'd bet that this is because we usually use "FindProfile()" (or something like that) and we just don't handle that properly.

# Steps to reproduce

- create a tab from the WT default settings
- import your custom settings
- duplicate the created tab

# Expected behavior

Not sure. Maybe a dialogue box saying "This operation could not be completed"?

# Actual behavior

CRASH!
comments: for the record, I don't think this was introduced in #2422, this probably dates back to pre-open source, when we started falling back to the default profiles if the settings were invalid. This just makes it more apparent, because we crash less aggressively.

:tada:This issue was addressed in #5090, which has now been successfully released as `Windows Terminal Preview v0.11.1121.0`.:tada:

Handy links:
* [Release Notes](https://github.com/microsoft/terminal/releases/tag/v0.11.1121.0)

review_comments: Should we actually duplicate a tab just by pushing its control's TerminalSettings object into another control? That might be even easier than a dialog, and more "expected"
So the related case is that of when you try to `{action:"newTab", "profile":"{guid-of-profile-that-doesnt-exist}"}` - in `TerminalPage::_OpenNewTab` - in _that_ case should there be a dialog?

Also that might be trickier. `TermControl` doesn't currently expose a way to retrieve it's `Settings` currently, nor does the `Pane` hang on to that `Settings` object after the control is initialized.

@DHowett-MSFT @cinnamon-msft necro'ing this PR. Lets come to a consensus, what should we do when the user tries to duplicate a tab for a tab with a profile that doesn't exist? 

1. I actually don't hate the idea of just duplicating the settings for the existing control. In that scenario, we'd probably just ignore the settings for that profile in the actual file, and just use whatever settings the control currently has. This might require some plumbing, but it's doable.
2. alternatively, we could display some sort of dialog to the user, though I'd want PM input on what that text should say.
3. Scenario 3, which is what I've currently got in this PR is "just silently do nothing".
I don't mind option 1 here. It's still what the user would expect. 😄
1 it is then :) I'll loop back around on this one (eventually)

Oooh this is actually much harder.

The connection _type_ is not a part of the `IControlSettings`, it's something that's instantiated separately. So we can get the control settings back out of the control for a control that doesn't have a valid profile anymore, but we won't be able to generate a new connection for that control.

Okay this is harder, but maybe not impossible, but probably impossible in v1.

The `Profile` knows how to build the connection settings, and the `ControlSettings`, etc. However, when the settings reloads like in this bug, we'll remove all the old profiles, and build a new list. 

If we wanted the case 1 behavior, we could wait until the `Profile` is a winrt object, then have each Pane hold a strong ref to the `Profile` that it's hosting. Then it would be trivial to be able to duplicate the settings from it. I believe that work is tracked in #3998.

How palatable is doing case 3 now (to fix the crash), then filing a follow up to do case 1 once #3998 is done?
